key_insight: Controlled, from‑scratch multimodal pretraining using the Transfusion framework (next‑token language + diffusion vision) reveals which design choices—data mix, objective weighting, and architectural coupling—drive multimodal learning, enabling principled trade‑offs without confounds from prior language pretraining.
problem_solved: Clarifies the opaque design space for native multimodal foundation models by isolating the core factors that govern joint language–vision pretraining, eliminating interference from preexisting language checkpoints.
method: Train multimodal models from scratch with the Transfusion setup: autoregressive next‑token loss for text and a diffusion objective for images.
Run controlled ablations that vary data composition, objective weighting (balance between language and vision losses), and architectural coupling (shared vs modality‑specific modules).
Evaluate cross‑modal and unimodal tasks to measure trade‑offs and identify which design choices most strongly affect downstream multimodal performance.
impact: Provides practical, experimentally grounded guidance for building native multimodal foundation models—reducing guesswork about architecture, data mixing, and loss balancing—and informs more efficient and effective model design for real-world multimodal applications.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Transfusion schematic showing text autoregressive path and image diffusion path with shared/adapter modules highlighted.
Bar/line chart: Ablation results comparing performance vs objective weighting and data mix (trade‑off curves).
Flowchart: Controlled experimental pipeline (from‑scratch pretraining → ablations → multimodal evaluations).
Icons/grid: Clear symbols for modalities (text, image), objectives (next‑token, diffusion), and outcomes (cross‑modal tasks).
paper_title: Beyond Language Modeling: An Exploration of Multimodal Pretraining
paper_authors: Shengbang Tong, David Fan, John Nguyen, Ellis Brown, Gaoyue Zhou
